title: Review: Scalars and vectors; Describing motion; Motion graphs; Constant-acceleration equations; Reference frames and relative motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: K01-1#N.10, K03-1#N.16, K05-1#N.3, MS05-1#N.13, K01-1#N.5, K03-1#N.5b, K05-1#N.16a, MS05-1#N.4, K01-1#N.2, MS05-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude only, such as speed, mass or energy.

items.label: Vector
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude and direction, such as force or momentum.

items.label: Components
items.clue: Two perpendicular parts that together replace the original arrow.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Runs from the first tail to the last tip when arrows are drawn tip to tail.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A toy car is released from rest on a straight slope and speeds up with constant acceleration. It travels 0.60 m in the first 2.0 s. How far does it travel between t = 4.0 s and t = 6.0 s?

A cyclist rides east at 6 m s⁻¹ relative to the road. Observer X stands beside the road. Observer Y is in a car that moves east along the same road at a constant 10 m s⁻¹. Which statement correctly compares the cyclist's velocity as measured by Y with the velocity measured by X?

options.text: Y measures the same velocity as X does, 6 m s⁻¹ east along the road.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, and in the opposite direction.
Y measures a larger speed than X does, and in the same direction.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, in the same direction.

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?

An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?
questions.explanation: The acceleration is constant, so the average velocity is halfway between 16 m s⁻¹ and 0: 8.0 m s⁻¹. Δx = 8.0 × 4.0 = 32 m. The same answer follows from Δx = v_x0 t + ½a_x t² with a_x = −4.0 m s⁻²: 64 − 32 = 32 m.

questions.stem: A moving walkway in an airport moves at constant velocity v_W relative to the floor. A passenger walks on the walkway with velocity v_P relative to the walkway. A worker walks on the floor beside the walkway at constant velocity v_F relative to the floor. All three velocities are components along the same straight line. Which expression gives the passenger's velocity as measured by the worker?

options.text: v_P − v_W − v_F
v_P + v_W + v_F
v_F − v_P − v_W
v_P + v_W − v_F

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?

A small block moves up a straight ramp inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Student 1 resolves the block's velocity into horizontal and vertical components. Student 2 resolves the same velocity using an x-axis along the ramp and a y-axis perpendicular to the ramp. Which statement about their results is correct?

options.text: Their components must match, since both pairs describe one velocity.
Their components differ, but each pair combines to give the same velocity.
Student 2's are not proper components, as components are horizontal and vertical.
Their components differ, so the two students find different speeds.
